name: Ataturk Alani and the Centre
tagline: The main square, where the whole city passes through
description: Trabzon's central square and the streets running off it hold the tea gardens, the shops, the banks and the bus connections, and the city's social life happens here rather than in bars. The Ottoman bazaar quarter and the harbour are both a short walk down the hill.
bestFor: Anyone who wants everything on foot and the bus network at the door
pros: All services, shops and transport within a few minutes
Best internet infrastructure in the city

name: Bosteppe and the Upper Slopes
tagline: Above the city, with the view back over the Black Sea
description: The residential slopes climbing behind the centre towards Boztepe, the hill that gives the classic view over Trabzon and the sea. Housing is newer apartment blocks stepped up the hillside, quieter than the coast road and with considerably better air and outlook.
bestFor: Stays that want the sea view and distance from the coastal highway
pros: Views over the city and the Black Sea
Cleaner air and much less traffic noise
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes down to the centre

name: Ortahisar and the Old Town
tagline: The walled Byzantine quarter above the ravine
description: The oldest part of Trabzon, enclosed by Byzantine walls on a ridge between two ravines, holding the Fatih mosque that was the city's cathedral and a dense grid of older houses. It is the most atmospheric quarter and the least modernised, ten minutes west of the main square.
bestFor: Stays that want the city's history rather than its shopping streets
pros: Byzantine walls and the old cathedral mosque
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Old housing stock in variable condition

name: Yomra and the Eastern Coast
tagline: East along the shore, newer blocks and lower rents
description: The coastal strip running east towards Yomra, where much of Trabzon's recent building has gone up: newer apartment blocks facing the sea, supermarkets and the university's outlying facilities. Rents are lower than the centre and the coast road takes fifteen to twenty minutes into town.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a newer flat with a sea view at a moderate rent
pros: Sea views for well below centre prices
Frequent minibuses along the coast road
cons: The coast highway runs between the blocks and the sea
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
Little to walk to in the evening

name: Akcaabat
tagline: The old town west along the bay, with the meatball and the harbour
description: A separate town about twelve kilometres west with its own harbour, an old quarter of Ottoman houses at Ortamahalle, and a national reputation for its kofte. It is quieter and cheaper than Trabzon, has a proper seafront and is connected by frequent minibuses along the coast.
bestFor: Quieter coastal stays with the city twenty minutes away
pros: Genuine old quarter and a working harbour
Quieter and more relaxed than the city
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes into Trabzon
